title: Placaeus distinguishes conditional and absolute power not to sin
source_text: XXX. Atque ut mentem suam clarius exponat vir ille Doctus, distinguit inter potentiam non peccandi & salutare bonum operandi conditionatam & absolutam. Potentiam non peccandi & bene operandi conditionatam vocat, per quam homo non peccare & bene operari potest si velit, & modo velit, sicut ipsum velle par est. Absolutam vero potentiam vocat, per quam homo simpliciter potest non peccare, & bene agere.
pass_a_gloss: XXX. And that that learned man may set forth his mind more clearly, he distinguishes between a conditional and an absolute power of not sinning and of working saving good. The conditional power of not sinning and of working well he calls that by which man can not sin and work well if he will, and provided he will, as it is right that he should will. But the absolute power he calls that by which man can simply not sin, and act well.
pass_b_english: To make his meaning plainer, that learned man separates a conditional from an absolute power of not sinning and of doing saving good.

The conditional power is the one by which a man is able to refrain from sin and do good if he wills, and on condition that he wills as he ought. The absolute power is the one by which a man simply is able to refrain from sin and to act well.

lemmas.latin: si velit, & modo velit, sicut ipsum velle par est
lemmas.gloss: if he will, and provided he will, as it is right that he should will

choices.why: The faculty of free decision; 'free choice' throughout, with 'freedom' for libertas.
